senses.gloss:
Vaitaraṇī
(‘[the river] to be crossed’)
------------------------------------------
The पुराणस् describe that those sinners who are destined to go to हेल्ल्, have to cross this foetid river, full of blood, hairs and bones. While crossing it they are tormented terribly.
It is also the name of a cow that is donated to a ब्राह्मण during the अन्त्येष्टि (death-rites), which is supposed to help the सोउल् of the dead to cross the river वैतरणी.
A river in कलिङ्ग (the modern Orissa State) has been called वैतरणी. It is sometimes identified either with the river Mahānadī or the Betrani.
The एकादशी of the dark fortnight of the month of Mārgaśīrṣā or Agrahāyaṇa (November/December) is called वैतरणी. A special vrata (religious observance) called Vaitaraṇīvrata is observed on this day by worshipping a dark cow so that it will help the observer to cross the वैतरणी River after death. This vrata has to be observed for one year in three periods of four months.
